newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency files complaint over grains contracts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency files complaint over grains contracts.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Wednesday it filed three complaints in its first action arising from an investigation of so-called hedge to arrive grain contracts.

The complaints were filed against Southern Thumb Co-op Inc., a cooperative grain elevator based in Lapeer, Mich., Grain Land Cooperative of Blue Earth, Minn., and Roger Wright, who operates from Mechanicsburg, Ohio, the CFTC said.

Hedge to arrive contracts blend aspects of traditional cash contracts and futures contracts, often allowing farmers to roll over the delivery date for grain. They have become popular in recent years and are meant to help farmers get better prices at harvest.

But the contracts have led to bitter disputes, with farmers claiming they were being compelled to deliver grains and some grain elevator companies saying farmers were refusing to deliver grains under the contracts.

CFTC enforcement director Geoffrey Aronow said the commission decided to file the complaints "because it has reason to believe that the contracts marketed, offered and entered into ... are illegal off-exchange futures or options contracts."
The agency charged Southern with violating rules against offering illegal, off-exchange agricultural options and with fraud related to the marketing of the illegal contracts, the agency said.
Grain Land was accused of offering and entering into illegal, off-exchange futures contracts, it said.
The case against Robert Wright involves fraud related to his marketing and promotion of illegal, off-exchange futures and options contracts, it said.

Also charged in the Wright case were A.G. Edwards and Sons Inc., a St. Louis, Miss., broker, Philip Luxenburger, an employee at the firm, and Buckeye Countrymark Inc., a Xenia, Ohio-based cooperative grain elevator, the agency said.

The broker and Luxenburger are charged with aiding Wright's alleged unregistered activities while Buckeye was accused of offering and entering into illegal, off-exchange futures and options contracts, CFTC said.
The administrative proceedings were aimed at finding out if the allegations are true and if so, what sanctions should be imposed, the CFTC said.
